div.head: II Cn 45.3
div.ab: Gyf hlaford his þeowan freolsdæge nyde to weorce, þolige þæs þeowan; ⁊ beo he syððan folcfrig; ⁊ gylde lahslit se hlaford mid Denum, wite mid Englum, be ðam þe seo dæd sig; oððe hine geladige.
Gyf laford his ðeowan freolsdæge nyde to weorce, ðolie ðæs ðeowan; ⁊ beo he syððan folcfrig; ⁊ gylde lahslit se laford mid Denum, wite mid Englum, bi ðam þe seo dæd sy; oððe geladie hine.
Gif hlaford his ðeowan freolsdage nyde to weorce, þolige þæs þeowan; ⁊ beo he syððan folcfrig; ⁊ gilde lahslit se hlaford mid Denum, wite mid Englum, be þam þe seo dæde sy; oððe geladige hine.
Si dominus cogat seruum suum festis diebus operari, ipsum seruum perdat; et sit deinceps publice liber; et soluat dominus láhslit cum Dacis, witam cum Anglis, secundum facti meritum; aut neget N.
Sin autem inuitus, domino suo pręcipiente, hoc fecerit, dominus careat seruo illo et det halsfang; seruus autem sit omnino liber; aut dominus purget se.

[45, 3] Si autem dominus seruum suum festo in[ui]tum operari compellat, amittat illum seruum; sitque liber populariter seruus ille; et dominus soluat legis transgressionem aput Danos, forisfacturam apud Anglos iuxta qualitatem facti; aut se purget.
Gyf laford his ðeowan freolsdæge nyde to weorce, ðolie ðæs ðeowan ⁊ beo he syððan folcfrig; ⁊ gylde lahslit se laford mid Denum, wite mid Englum, bi ðam þe seo dæd sy; oððe geladie hine.
Gyf hlaford his þeowan freolsdæge nyde to weorce, þolige þæs þeowan, and beo he syððan folcfrig; and gylde lahslit se hlaford mid Denum, wite mid Englum, be ðam þe seo dæd sig, oððe hine geladige.

Wenn ein Herr seinen Sklaven am Feiertage zur Arbeit zwingt, verliere er den Sklaven; und sei dieser fortan volks- [landrechtlich] frei; und zahle der Herr Rechtsbruchbusse bei den Dänen, Strafgeld bei den Engländern, je nachdem die That ist; oder er schwöre sich rein.

If a lord compels his slave to work on a feast-day, let him lose the slave; and let the latter thereafter be free [in folk-law]; and let the lord pay lahslit among the Danes, a fine among the English, according to what the deed is; or let him clear himself.

If a lord compels his slave to work during a church festival, he shall lose the slave, who shall henceforth obtain the rights of a freeman, and the lord shall pay lahslit in a Danish district and a fine in an English one, according to the nature of the offence, or else he shall clear himself.

If a master compels his slave to work on a feast-day, he is to forfeit the slave, who is afterwards to be a free man; and the master is to pay lahslit among the Danes, a fine among the English, in proportion to the deed; or to clear himself.

If a lord compels his slave to work on a holy day, he shall lose the slave, who will be free thenceforth; and he must pay lahslit within the Danelaw and a penalty among the English according to the nature of the deed; or he must exonerate himself.
